newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses mixed, quiet as U.S. data looms.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses mixed, quiet as U.S. data looms.

text.p: European stock markets were treading water at midsession on Thursday, awaiting a wave of U.S. economic indicators this afternoon which will test yet again whether the buoyant U.S. economy can grow rapidly without surging demand leaking into higher inflation.

London shares lost most early gains, and U.S. shares in London traded quietly firmer. The Paris bourse was mixed, while Germany recouped some earlier losses which were prompted by dealers adjusting prices for the 33-point fall on Wall Street on Wednesday.
"The market is quietly higher in anticipation of good numbers, especially given the lack of news on the corporate side," said one London broker.
The dollar was steady at slightly higher levels after a sharp fall on Wednesday on market expectations of higher German interest rates
As Wall Street has swept ever higher throughout the year, the market consequences of disappointing economic data become ever more worrying.

After more benign than expected U.S. Producer Prices for July released on Wednesday, investors were awaiting confirmation of the trend in July Consumer Prices, due at 1230 GMT and expected to show a 0.2 percent rise.
The flood of data includes industrial production and business inventories for June, July real earnings and money supply figures.

The reports will be among the data considered by Federal Reserve policymakers next week when they decide whether economic growth is strong enough to require a rise in interest rates in a pre-emptive move against inflation.

If consumer prices emerge sharply higher than expected, it will drag shares lower and could even mark the high-water point of the aged bull market. But if it confirms Wednesday's producer price data it could sweep equities to even loftier levels as the U.S. economy races ahead with barely a ripple of inflation.

London's FTSE-100 index of leading shares was just 6.1 points higher, having shed early gains of over 20 points. However traders remain doubly relieved that the market had held above the psychological 5,000 points on Wednesday and that Wall Street's decline was just 33 points, ending at 7,928.32, after having been 75 points lower at one time.

"A few buyers came in first thing but it has gone very quiet now," a trader said. "People are wary of the wobbles on Wall Street but after a couple of bad days here there does seem to be support at the 5,000 level."
U.S Treasury bonds in London maintained their firmer tone after a volatile day on Wednesday.

German shares fell 1.10 percent in bourse trade, catching up with the declines on Wall Street late on Wednesday. Some dealers expected a further decline in the electronic IBIS-DAX market in the lead-up to the U.S. data.

In Paris, shares began a shade higher after a 2.5 percent drop on Wednesday, but then slid below their Wednesday level. Dealers expected any upside to be limited by the end of the day as investors squared their books and packed up for the mid-August long weekend.
European investors were nervous of buying U.S. stocks ahead of the economic data, with a strong dollar compounding the worry over demanding price-earnings ratios.
"The other thing is the currency," a sharedealer said. "The strength of the dollar has made Wall Street very expensive...too expensive."
Foreign exchange dealers said longer term sentiment on the dollar remains positive, but ponder whether the dollar will have to shed more ground before accelerating higher again.
"There is a small rebound this morning but the market is leaning a bit more towards the downside in the short term," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The pound, whose recent burst of strength has hit British exporters, briefly fell below 2.90 marks as the German currency rose.
"The main theme in continental Europe is German rate fears...That should give the deutschemark some support," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.
But the mark was off peaks scaled on Wednesday after the Bundesbank warned the pace of inflation had picked up and amid fresh talk of a delay to European economic and monetary union.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted around 1.8325 marks and 116.36 yen, compared with 1.8547 and 115.80 in late European trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 6.5 points at 5,010.1.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was down 47.05 points at 4,234.56
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was down 3.79 at 2,920.05.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was $1.10 an ounce firmer in London at $327.30. Silver was fixed two cents firmer at $4.48.
